newsitem.title: GERMANY: Iran says Netanyahu blocking Arad release - FAZ.
newsitem.headline: Iran says Netanyahu blocking Arad release - FAZ.

text.p: A leading German newspaper quoted senior Iranian sources on Thursday accusing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of delaying a solution to the case of the Israeli airman Ron Arad, missing since 1986.

The Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung (FAZ), in a bylined report from Tehran, quoted the Iranians as saying Netanyahu had taken a tough line in negotiations and thus made a solution before the end of this year impossible.

The newspaper said Syria had hinted to Tehran Arad might still be alive and that Damascus -- and not Lebanese groups as previously suspected -- might hold the key to solving the mystery. But it gave no proof Arad was not dead, it said.
"The Ron Arad case cannot be closed by the end of the year as originally planned because of Netanyahu's stubborn stand," the newspaper quoted "circles close to the Iranian government" as saying.

"If our information from Damascus is correct that Arad may still be alive or the location of his corpse is known, then the talks should not be drawn out because of Israel's tough line," it went on to quote the sources as saying.
The sources told the FAZ that an envoy of Netanyahu had rejected a key Syrian demand that, if he were released, Arad must not say anything about where he was held.
Syria demanded this so that it could not be branded as an accomplice of those holding Arad hostage, it said.
The newspaper added: "There were apparently no hints that Syria had demanded an Israeli retreat from the Golan Heights in connection with the talks about Arad."
Israel has said it believes Arad, who was shot down over Lebanon in 1986, is being held in Iran.

German intelligence coordinator Bernd Schmidbauer, who coordinated a swap of fallen soldiers' remains between Israel and Lebanon in July and has been in contact with all sides in the Arad case, has said he believes the pilot is alive.
The Frankfurter Allgemeine quoted Schmidbauer as telling it on Wednesday: "I will not give up hope that the efforts to solve this humanitarian case will still be successful."

The FAZ quoted the Tehran sources as saying the Arad case was being handled directly by the office of President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and it was therefore correct for other Iranian officials to say they had no information on the case.
The Tehran sources told the newspaper the Arad mystery was near to being solved before Netanyahu took office but that prospects had dimmed since then.
They quoted Syrian negotiators as saying they thought the new Israeli government had "not the slightest interest in clearing up this humanitarian case."
The FAZ report was written by Udo Ulfkotte, who has been following the Arad case closely.
Former Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin rushed to Bonn in March 1995 to meet Chancellor Helmut Kohl after he reported Germany was brokering a deal on Arad between Israel and Iran.
The report provoked charges in Israel that Germany sought a deal to dampen criticism of its continued trade and "critical dialogue" with Iran.

Israeli media reports said Kohl, angered when Rabin apparently passed those charges on in a telephone conversation, threatened to cancel his trip. Rabin's lightning visit cleared the air and Kohl's trip went ahead.
